question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

31, 94, 283, ?, 2551, 7654, 22963
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 850.

GIVEN

• 31, 94, 283, ?, 2551, 7654, 22963

SOLUTION

• The rule is ×3 + 1 each time.

• 31×3+1 = 94; 94×3+1 = 283; 283×3+1 = 850; 850×3+1 = 2551; 2551×3+1 = 7654; 7654×3+1 = 22963.

• Missing term = 850.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Check the ratio: each term is roughly 3× the previous. Multiply by 3 and add 1 — 283×3 = 849, +1 = 850.

NOTE

• For fast-growing series, test ×2, ×3 (±1, ±2) patterns first before trying differences.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

PD : VJ :: ? : DX :: YK : EQ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. XR.

GIVEN

• PD : VJ :: ? : DX :: YK : EQ

SOLUTION

• Rule (first→second): add +6 to each letter. P(16)+6=V(22), D(4)+6=J(10). ✓

• Check (fifth→sixth): Y(25)+6=E(31−26=5), K(11)+6=Q(17). ✓

• So answer +6 = DX ⇒ answer = DX − 6: D(4)−6=X(24), X(24)−6=R(18) ⇒ XR.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Both known pairs add +6. Reverse it on DX (subtract 6) to get the missing cluster: X, R.

NOTE

• Use position numbers A=1…Z=26 and wrap around 26 for +/− letter shifts.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

DB, ?, VP, RJ, ND, JX, FR, BL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. ZV.

GIVEN

• DB, ?, VP, RJ, ND, JX, FR, BL

SOLUTION

• First letters: D, ?, V, R, N, J, F, B → each −4: D(4)→Z(26)→V(22)→R(18)→N(14)→J(10)→F(6)→B(2). So ? starts with Z.

• Second letters: B, ?, P, J, D, X, R, L → each −6: B(2)→V(22)→P(16)→J(10)→D(4)→X(24)→R(18)→L(12). So ? ends with V.

• Missing term = ZV.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Split into first-letter (−4) and second-letter (−6) chains; the 2nd term is Z and V.

NOTE

• In two-letter series, always separate the two columns and find each step independently.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(XR, VM, TH)

(IN, GI, ED)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (FI, DD, BY).

GIVEN

• (XR, VM, TH)

SOLUTION

• First letters: X(24), V(22), T(20) → −2 each.

• Second letters: R(18), M(13), H(8) → −5 each.

• Apply to option 2: F(6),D(4),B(2) → −2 each ✓; I(9),D(4),Y(9−5=4−5=−1→25) → −5 each ✓.

• So (FI, DD, BY) follows the same rule.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the step: 1st letters drop by 2, 2nd letters drop by 5. Only (FI, DD, BY) fits both.

NOTE

• Verify the pattern on all three clusters of an option before selecting.

question: If 12 March 2024 is a Tuesday, then what day will 21 September 2024 be?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Saturday.

GIVEN

• 12 March 2024 = Tuesday; find the day on 21 September 2024 (2024 is a leap year).

SOLUTION

• Days from 12 Mar to 12 Sep = 19(Mar)+30+31+30+31+31 = 172, then +9 to reach 21 Sep = 184 + 9? Counting month-to-month: Mar12→Sep12 = 184 days, Sep12→Sep21 = 9 days ⇒ total 193 days.

• 193 ÷ 7 = 27 remainder 4 odd days.

• Tuesday + 4 = Saturday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the remainder (odd days) matters: 193 mod 7 = 4 ⇒ add 4 days to Tuesday → Saturday.

NOTE

• Odd days: divide total days by 7; add the remainder to the given weekday.

question: If 14 October 1988 was Friday, then what day was it on 14 February 1989?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Tuesday.

GIVEN

• 14 October 1988 = Friday; find the day on 14 February 1989.

SOLUTION

• Same date each month, so count full months: Oct14→Nov14 = 31, Nov14→Dec14 = 30, Dec14→Jan14 = 31, Jan14→Feb14 = 31 ⇒ 123 days.

• 123 ÷ 7 = 17 remainder 4 odd days.

• Friday + 4 = Tuesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 123 mod 7 = 4 → jump 4 weekdays from Friday: Sat, Sun, Mon, Tue.

NOTE

• Add the days of each month between the two same-dates, then take mod 7.

question: 5 boys G, H, J, K and L are sitting in a row facing south (not necessarily in the same order). G is to the immediate right of K. H is to the immediate left of J. L is in the middle of the row. H is to the left of L. Who is sitting at second position from the left end of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. J.

GIVEN

• 5 boys face south; G right of K; H left of J; L in middle; H left of L.

SOLUTION

• Facing south, a person's left = East, right = West. Numbering West→East as 1–5: 'right' = lower number.

• L in middle = position 3. H is left of L (East) and J is immediately right (West) of H ⇒ J=4, H=5.

• G immediately right (West) of K with the two left seats ⇒ G=1, K=2.

• Order (West→East): G, K, L, J, H. The left end (facing south) is the East side (pos 5); second from left end = pos 4 = J.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For south-facing rows, flip left/right — the row's 'left end' is the reader's right side; the 2nd such seat holds J.

NOTE

• Facing south: your right hand points West, left hand East (mirror of facing north).

question: 7 girls A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). D sits fifth to the right of A. D does not sit at any of the extreme ends of the row. F sits exactly in the middle of row. Two girls sit between F and B. G is third to the left of E. Who are sitting at the extreme ends of the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. A and B.

GIVEN

• 7 girls face north; D fifth to right of A; D not at ends; F in middle; two girls between F and B; G third to left of E.

SOLUTION

• Facing north, number 1–7 left→right. D = A+5; since D≠end ⇒ A=1, D=6.

• F in middle = 4. Two girls between F(4) and B ⇒ B = 7.

• G third to left of E ⇒ E=5, G=2, leaving C=3.

• Order: A(1), G(2), C(3), F(4), E(5), D(6), B(7). Ends = A and B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 'Fifth to the right' with 7 seats forces A=1, D=6; the far ends then fall to A and B.

NOTE

• Fix the strongest clue (largest gap) first, then place middle and relative clues.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option.

GIVEN

• Figure-1 (8, □ / □, 5) is related to Figure-2 (□, 8 / 5, □); find the figure related to Figure-3 (□, V / D, B).

SOLUTION

• Figure-1 → Figure-2 is a left–right mirror (lateral inversion): the two columns swap, so 8□/□5 becomes □8/5□.

• Apply the same mirror to Figure-3 (□V / DB): swapping columns gives V□ / BD.

• This matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just swap the left and right entries of each row of the third box — top row V□, bottom row BD.

NOTE

• A vertical (left–right) mirror interchanges the left and right positions while keeping top/bottom fixed.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option.

GIVEN

• Figure-1 (a shape with 5 outward arrows/rays) relates to Figure-2 (5 crosses '×'); find the figure related to Figure-3 (an inner square with 6 outward arrows).

SOLUTION

• Rule: the number of arrows/rays in the first figure equals the number of small symbols drawn in its partner.

• Figure-1 has 5 arrows → Figure-2 has 5 crosses. ✓

• Figure-3 has 6 outward arrows → its partner must have 6 symbols (six '+' signs).

• Option shows exactly six plus-signs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count the arrows in the given figure (6) and pick the option with that many marks.

NOTE

• Element-counting analogies: match the quantity of a repeated feature, not its shape.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first number in the same way as the fourth number is related to the third number and sixth number is related to the fifth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

3290 : ? :: 59 : 9 :: 6295 : 6245
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3240.

GIVEN

• 3290 : ? :: 59 : 9 :: 6295 : 6245

SOLUTION

• Find the operation from the known pairs: 59 − 9 = 50 and 6295 − 6245 = 50.

• So each 'related' number is obtained by subtracting 50.

• 3290 − 50 = 3240.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference in both given pairs is a constant 50 ⇒ 3290 − 50 = 3240.

NOTE

• Treat numbers as wholes (per the note); test constant difference/ratio first.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

357 : 719 :: ? : 1263 :: 451 : 907
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 629.

GIVEN

• 357 : 719 :: ? : 1263 :: 451 : 907

SOLUTION

• Rule (number → related): ×2 + 5. Check: 357×2+5 = 719 ✓; 451×2+5 = 907 ✓.

• So ? ×2 + 5 = 1263 ⇒ ?×2 = 1258 ⇒ ? = 629.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the rule on 1263: (1263 − 5) ÷ 2 = 629.

NOTE

• If the second number is a bit more than double the first, test ×2 + k.

question: In a certain code language, 'TOWEL' is coded as '201523512' and 'SOAP' is coded as '1915116'. How will 'MATTER' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1312020518.

GIVEN

• TOWEL → 201523512; SOAP → 1915116.

SOLUTION

• Each letter is replaced by its alphabet position and written together.

• TOWEL = 20-15-23-5-12 = 201523512 ✓; SOAP = 19-15-1-16 = 1915116 ✓.

• MATTER = M-A-T-T-E-R = 13-1-20-20-5-18 = 1312020518.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just string the position numbers: M=13, A=1, T=20, T=20, E=5, R=18.

NOTE

• Position code: A=1 … Z=26; single-digit letters (A–I) add no leading zero here.

question: In a certain coded language 'LOVED' is coded as 'NTTBY' and 'KNUBS' is coded as 'MSSYN'. How will 'HALVE' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. JFJSZ.

GIVEN

• LOVED → NTTBY; KNUBS → MSSYN.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise shifts: 1st +2, 2nd +5, 3rd −2, 4th −3, 5th −5.

• Check LOVED: L+2=N, O+5=T, V−2=T, E−3=B, D−5=Y ✓. (KNUBS also fits.)

• HALVE: H(8)+2=J, A(1)+5=F, L(12)−2=J, V(22)−3=S, E(5)−5=Z ⇒ JFJSZ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the shift pattern (+2, +5, −2, −3, −5) from LOVED and apply directly.

NOTE

• Positional codes need not use one fixed shift — check each letter's own shift.

question: At what time (in PM), the angle between hour and minute hands of a clock will be 70 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5:40.

GIVEN

• Angle between the hands = 70°.

SOLUTION

• Angle = |30H − 5.5M|.

• At 5:40: |30×5 − 5.5×40| = |150 − 220| = 70°. ✓

• Others: 6:45→67.5°, 2:30→105°, 3:35→102.5° — none is 70°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Plug each option into |30H − 5.5M|; 5:40 gives exactly 70°.

NOTE

• Hour hand = 30° per hour + 0.5° per min; minute hand = 6° per min ⇒ formula |30H − 5.5M|.

question: A clock is 4 minutes slow at 8:20 AM and 8 minutes fast at 2:50 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 10:30.

GIVEN

• At 8:20 AM clock is 4 min slow; at 2:50 PM it is 8 min fast.

SOLUTION

• Total real time from 8:20 AM to 2:50 PM = 6 h 30 min = 390 minutes.

• Total gain over this span = 4 + 8 = 12 minutes (from −4 to +8).

• To be correct it must gain 4 min (reach 0). Time needed = 390 × 4/12 = 130 min = 2 h 10 min.

• 8:20 AM + 2 h 10 min = 10:30 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Clock gains uniformly: fraction to cancel slowness = 4/12 of 390 min = 130 min after 8:20.

NOTE

• Correct-time instant: real time × (initial error ÷ total error swing), added to the start.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option.

GIVEN

• A 4-figure series of a 'lens/magnifier' and a 'key' inside a box, with the '?' to be filled as the 5th figure.

SOLUTION

• Across the series the two objects steadily move upward and rotate, shifting from the bottom of the box toward the top row.

• Continuing that motion, in the 5th figure both objects reach the top of the box — magnifier at the top-left and key at the top-right.

• This matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Track the upward drift of each object; the next step lands both on the top edge → Option.

NOTE

• In figure series, watch position (movement), orientation (rotation) and shape separately.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option.

GIVEN

• A 4-figure series of three shaded boxes hanging on a branching 'tree' of lines; the 5th figure (?) is required.

SOLUTION

• From figure to figure the three boxes and their small branch-ticks shift/rotate along the stem in a fixed cycle (the heights of the boxes step down left→right and the tick pattern advances).

• Continuing the cycle, the 5th figure has the tall box at top-left, the middle box lower, and the small box at bottom-right — the arrangement shown in Option.

• This matches Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Follow the descending 'staircase' of boxes and the moving branch-ticks; the next stage is Option.

NOTE

• For repeating figure series, identify the cycle length and extend it by one step.

question: The ratio of present ages of N and R is 5 : 3. After 4 years, their ages will be in the ratio of 3 : 2. What is the present age of R?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 12 years.

GIVEN

• Present N : R = 5 : 3; after 4 years N : R = 3 : 2.

SOLUTION

• Let N = 5x, R = 3x. Then (5x+4)/(3x+4) = 3/2.

• 2(5x+4) = 3(3x+4) ⇒ 10x + 8 = 9x + 12 ⇒ x = 4.

• R = 3x = 3×4 = 12 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Cross-multiply once: 10x+8 = 9x+12 → x = 4 → R = 3×4 = 12.

NOTE

• Age-ratio problems: set common multiple x, add the years to both, then cross-multiply.

question: Father's age 30 years ago from present was 4 times of the age of his son 9 years ago from present. Son's age after 14 years from present is 24 years. What is the ratio of present ages of father and son?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 17 : 5.

GIVEN

• (Father − 30) = 4 × (Son − 9); Son + 14 = 24.

SOLUTION

• Son + 14 = 24 ⇒ present Son = 10.

• Son 9 years ago = 10 − 9 = 1.

• Father 30 years ago = 4 × 1 = 4 ⇒ present Father = 4 + 30 = 34.

• Ratio Father : Son = 34 : 10 = 17 : 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Get son's present age first (24 − 14 = 10), then back-calculate the father: 4×1 + 30 = 34 ⇒ 17:5.

NOTE

• Convert each clue to present age immediately, then form the ratio and simplify.
